answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed when a challenge proves coordinated fraud; influence also grows only with time and verified, independent transactions, not account count. A velvet invitation or falcon profile earns no extra weight, and a shale-backed bond is still capital at risk: an attacker must lock funds in every Sybil account, sustain distinct activity, and lose deposits when links are exposed, making mass identities costly rather than free.
